assessment.summary: SERPINE1 (PAI-1) is a secreted inhibitor of tPA and uPA with a role in senescence. About 21% of its literature concerns ageing, and it is associated with cardiometabolic and neurodegenerative disease. MR shows that genetically higher PAI-1 is associated with worse parental longevity (Bonferroni significant), which supports inhibition. This rests on one cis variant with inconclusive colocalisation, and the frailty and GrimAge outcomes are null. It is tractable by both small molecules and antibodies, but clinical precedence is limited to one Phase 1 drug. Bleeding risk is the main safety concern. I recommend that we prioritise it.
key_uncertainties: Colocalisation for parental longevity is inconclusive (PP.H4 0.13, PP.H1 0.83), so the shared causal variant is unconfirmed.
The MR uses a single instrument, so pleiotropy cannot be tested.
Replication of the instrument's effect on protein level is mixed (gilly2020 p=0.012; sun2018_somascan p=0.15).
Bleeding and thrombosis trade-offs of chronic PAI-1 inhibition in healthy older people are unknown.
